title: Bidirectional Dijkstra on Singapore: Scale Routing ⚡
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra visually split the search: one wave from the start, another from the destination, meeting in the middle for faster shortest paths. This is how route planning engines reduce work while still guaranteeing optimal routes.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional Dijkstra: How Modern Route Planners Scale ⚡ — Inside high-scale navigation engines, the shortest path search runs from both ends at once.

Here’s what you’re seeing on the Singapore grid:
1) Start-side Dijkstra expands outward until it’s “close enough” to the goal-side wave.
2) Goal-side Dijkstra does the same in reverse.
3) The algorithm stops when the best known forward+backward connection can’t be improved.

✅ Why it’s faster at scale: instead of exploring the whole graph from the start, you roughly halve the search depth (often a big win on large maps).

Takeaway: If you can run the problem from source and target simultaneously, you can cut the explored frontier without losing correctness.

Debate question: In your projects, would bidirectional search beat heuristics (like A*) more often—or do they complement each other?

Mechanics (fast & correct):
